newsitem.title: USA: Armand Hammer "master of deception" article says.
newsitem.headline: Armand Hammer "master of deception" article says.

text.p: Industralist Armand Hammer spent the last days of his life cutting his son, mistresses and illegitimate daughter out of his will because he feared a lawsuit would force his deepest secrets into the open, the New Yorker magazine reported Monday.

In an article written by Edward Jay Epstein, whose full scale biography of the late head of Occidental Petroleum will appear later this month, Hammer's last days are presented as the culmination of a lifetime of deception and double-crosses.
Pretending to be a billionaire, Hammer left an estate of a far more modest $40 million when he died in 1990 at age 92 and large amounts of that was contested, Epstein said.

When Hammer learned that he was being sued by the estate of his late wife on the grounds that he had looted her personal fortune, he frantically gutted the financial guarantees he made for two long-time mistresses, his son and his illegitimate daughter so that his secrets would not be made public.

Epstein said Hammer, who boasted of his connections to American presidents and Soviet leaders, had one mistress change her name and identity so his wife would not become suspicious of her and he had another move to Mexico City and adopt a false name there.
The upshot was that both women, his son and daughter had to sue the estate.
